greek.forms: Nom: σοφία / σοφίαι; Gen: σοφίας / σοφιῶν; Dat: σοφίᾳ / σοφίαις; Acc: σοφίαν / σοφίας
greek.etymology: From σοφός (wise) + -ία (abstract noun suffix). English descendants: philosophy (love of wisdom), sophisticated (worldly-wise), sophomore (wise fool, σοφός + μωρός), theosophy (divine wisdom).
greek.usage_example: ὁ φιλόσοφος τῆς σοφίας ἐπιθυμητής — The philosopher is a lover of wisdom
greek.did_you_know: The Seven Sages of Greece each contributed a maxim to Apollo's temple at Delphi, but 'σοφία' originally meant practical skill - a master craftsman was σοφός. Plato elevated it from technical expertise to philosophical wisdom, forever changing how we understand the word.
